subject: Committed capacity options & ramp scenarios (Sunbeam AI)
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Evan Liu <evan.liu@sunbeam.ai>
Cc: Priya Anand <priya@sunbeam.ai>
Date: 2027-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Committed capacity options & ramp scenarios (Sunbeam AI)

Hi Evan / Priya,

Thanks again for the call this morning — really excited about Sunbeam's plans to expand the real-time summarization feature. Per our discussion, I attached a concise proposal that lays out three committed-capacity options and plausible month-by-month ramp profiles so you can see the unit economics and latency tradeoffs. High level:

- Option A (Conservative): 8 GPUs minimum (NVIDIA H100 equivalent), steady-state by month 2. Good fit if you want predictable spend and quick time-to-serve.
- Option B (Balanced): 16 GPUs minimum, phased ramp (8 → 12 → 16 across three months) with 2× burst pools. Better for moderate growth and lower P50 latency.
- Option C (Aggressive): 32 GPUs minimum, 1-month ramp to full capacity, includes dedicated burst pool and regional mirroring (US + EU). Best for performance-sensitive use cases and aggressive SLAs.

Key assumptions used in the attachment: typical sequence length 256 tokens, 40% cache hit on prefixes, 60 req/s baseline traffic for month 1 with 3× peak spikes. Pricing shown is committed-monthly billing with optional burst overage billing and an SLA addendum.

Next steps I propose: 1) you review the attached PDF and pick 1–2 options you want detailed into an SOW; 2) we align on ramp timing and region (we can mirror to EU later if needed); 3) we schedule a follow-up where Rishi can sign off on perf tuning and memory footprint.

I left a couple illustrative cost scenarios on page 4. If you want quicker throughput with lower per-token cost we can push quantization + larger batching, but that will increase cold-start tail latency — happy to walk through tradeoffs.

Best,

Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0143

Attachments: Sunbeam_AI_Dedicated_Proposal_v1.pdf
From: Evan Liu <evan.liu@sunbeam.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Anand <priya@sunbeam.ai>
Date: 2027-04-12T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Committed capacity options & ramp scenarios (Sunbeam AI)

Sean — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear options. A few clarifying questions after skimming:

1) For Option B, what is the minimum burst capacity you're guaranteeing? We saw inconsistent tail behavior with burst pools at another vendor and want to avoid that.
2) For Option A, can we start with a smaller trial (4 GPUs) for 4 weeks before committing? We have a short campaign in May and want to validate the cache heuristics first.
3) Do any of the options include a failover to a lower-cost model family if the cluster is saturated? We need graceful degradation for peak times.

Also, curious about the regional mirror in Option C — what's the incremental latency and cost for the EU replica?

Would prefer to talk live — can you do a 30-min slot tomorrow at 11am PT?

Thanks,
Evan
VP of Product, Sunbeam AI
Evan Liu <evan.liu@sunbeam.ai>

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-04-12T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Committed capacity options & ramp scenarios (internal recommendations)

Sean / Rishi — internal note before the call with Sunbeam:

I reviewed Evan's questions and the numbers in the PDF. My recommendation to present tomorrow:

- Accept the 4-GPU trial for 4 weeks but frame it as a pre-commit pilot with clear success criteria (95th pct latency under 500ms on 256-token sequences and cache hit >=30%). Pilot will use Option A hardware but with optimized batching.
- For Option B burst guarantees: propose a burst pool sized at 50% of committed capacity with preemptible nodes and a 5-minute warm path. In the SOW we should include a capacity fallback policy that routes to a compatible quantized variant (same model family, 8-bit) if burst capacity is exhausted. That addresses the graceful degradation ask.
- EU mirror: incremental cost estimate is ~+30% of US cluster OPEX (network + reserved capacity). Latency typically +30–60ms for the replica based on our RU tests.

I've annotated the PDF with these suggestions and added a short SLA addendum (Sunbeam_SLA_Addendum.docx) for the failover/fallback behavior.

If Rishi can confirm the memory / KV cache assumptions match the model they plan to serve, we can lock the month-by-month ramp in the SOW.

—Marissa
Director, Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: Sunbeam_SLA_Addendum.docx

Evan / Priya — thanks for the questions and great timing. We're available 2027-04-13 11:00am PT and have blocked 30 minutes. I've attached an updated package that reflects Marissa's internal recommendations and includes the SLA addendum and two ramp templates (conservative and balanced).

Quick answers up front:
- Option B burst pool: we'll size a burst pool at 50% of the committed GPUs. Burst is backed by preemptible nodes + fast warm-up; we'll include a burst eviction policy and a routing fallback to a compatible 8-bit quantized variant if the pool is exhausted.
- 4-GPU trial: we can run a time-boxed pilot for 4 weeks. We will measure the success criteria jointly (95th pct latency, cache hit). Pilot credits and pro-rated billing are spelled out on page 3.
- EU mirror: estimated +30% OPEX (network + reserved dfwd). Latency impact typically 30–60ms.

Next actions:
1) Please confirm the 11am PT slot for 2027-04-13.
2) If you want the 4-GPU pilot, reply with the requested start date (we can provision within 48 hours once you sign the pilot SOW).
3) If you want us to produce a tailored SOW for Option B (balanced) we can deliver a draft by EOD Friday.
